    Cartan matrices from finite idempotent families #

    For a finite family e in a finite-dimensional algebra, the (i,j) corner is e i * A * e j. Its dimension is the usual split-basic left-module Cartan entry. This file packages that matrix and proves that it is preserved when an algebra equivalence transports the idempotent family.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.idempotentCorner {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type u_1} (e : ι → A) (i j : ι) :
    Submodule k A

    The vector subspace e i * A * e j, presented as the range of the corresponding two-sided multiplication map.

          theorem LargeIndecomposable.idempotentCartanMatrix_map {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {B : Type w} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (f : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (e : ι → A) :

          Transporting a finite idempotent family through an algebra equivalence does not change its Cartan matrix.

          theorem LargeIndecomposable.det_idempotentCartanMatrix_map {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {B : Type w} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (e : ι → A) :
          (idempotentCartanMatrix fun (r : ι) => f (e r)).det = (idempotentCartanMatrix e).det

          In particular, the determinant of an idempotent Cartan matrix is unchanged by algebra equivalence.
